claim.quote: These data provide new direct detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for WIMP masses >20 GeV/c$^{2}$ and demonstrate significant sensitivity for spin-independent interactions.

key_value_text.note: The paper states its limit as plotted curves, the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section against WIMP mass (Fig. 6, drawn with a band for the systematic uncertainty in the fluorine bubble-nucleation efficiency) and the spin-independent one (Fig. 7), and gives no single cross-section number, so `key_value` stays empty. The 'total exposure of 553 kg-days' of the abstract, which the record used as its key value until 2026-10-29, is in `summary.technical`.
key_value_text.quote: The 90% C.L. limit for this result is shown in blue, interpreting all 20 observed single recoil events as WIMP candidates with no background subtraction.
key_value_text.value: The 90% C.L. spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit is the curve of Fig. 6, with all 20 observed single recoil events treated as WIMP candidates and no background subtraction.

name: First dark matter search results from a 4-kg CF$_3$I bubble chamber operated in a deep underground site
notes: The arXiv listing's abstract still reads 'world best direct detection constraints'; the paper itself (v2, 19 Sep 2012) says 'new direct detection constraints' and reports an additional background; the record follows the paper (2026-10-29).

summary.plain: The same chamber, moved two kilometres underground to SNOLAB with 4.0 kg of CF3I, set new limits on spin-dependent WIMP-proton scattering for heavier WIMPs. It also saw more single-bubble events than its known neutron background explains, with signs of a further background.
summary.technical: 4.0 kg CF3I in the SNOLAB J-Drift, September 2010-August 2011: 553 kg-days over three nucleation thresholds (437.4 kg-days effective for single bubbles); 20 single nuclear-recoil candidates and 3 multiple-bubble events; an internal neutron background estimated to account for five single-recoil events; alpha rejection >99.3%; the remaining excess of single-bubble events shows characteristics of an additional background (Phys. Rev. D 86, 052001).

title: First dark matter search results from a 4-kg CF$_3$I bubble chamber operated in a deep underground site
why_it_matters: The paper reports new direct-detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for WIMP masses above 20 GeV/c^2 from a deep underground site, and an excess of single-bubble events whose characteristics indicate an additional background.
